## Discovered work filed — and why this ticket is BLOCKED on it

Filed `irongrey-chubby-oxpecker` (`aa7b-5e47-6d3d-4615`, P1 bug), linked `discovered_from` this ticket:
**"Outbound comment sync is not idempotent — ~205 comments re-posted to Jira every hourly pass"**.

That is the real defect. This canary ticket cannot go green until it is fixed, because the cap
refusal on REB-1861 is produced by the duplication loop and will keep being produced.

**No code change has been made.** The remediation is materially larger than this bug's scope and
involves ongoing writes to production Jira, so it is escalated to the operator for a decision
before anything is implemented. Two candidate scopes, deliberately kept separate:

1. **Fix the duplication loop** (`irongrey-chubby-oxpecker`) — the actual cause. Needs runtime
   evidence first to establish which dedup layer fails; do not fix from static reading.
2. **Harden the cap classification** (separate, optional) — treat `COMMENTS_PER_ISSUE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`
   as a designed skip rather than a per-mutation failure, per the project's own skip-vs-failure
   split (ticket a3fa) and the hierarchy-rejection precedent (`dispatch_one.py:525-558`). This
   would make the bridge green again **without** fixing the duplication — which is why it must not
   be done alone: it would silence the alarm while ~4,920 duplicate comments/day keep landing.

**Operator decision needed:** whether to pause reconcile-bridge.yml to stop the bleed while the
idempotency fix is developed. Every hour it runs adds ~205 duplicate comments across 28 issues and
pushes the next issue (REB-1580, ~10 days out) toward the same cap.

This ticket stays open and claimed; it auto-closes on the next successful reconcile-bridge run.
